name: Crambin

focal_points.name: Alpha-helix bundle
focal_points.description: Two parallel alpha-helices forming the core hydrophobic scaffold

focal_points.name: Disulfide bridges
focal_points.description: Three disulfide bonds (Cys3-Cys40, Cys4-Cys32, Cys16-Cys26) stabilizing the fold

focal_points.name: Beta-sheet region
focal_points.description: Small antiparallel beta-sheet at the C-terminal end

composition_notes: Slight tilt around Y-axis reveals all three structural elements simultaneously. At 46 residues, crambin fits well as a compact reference structure in multi-panel layouts.

name: B-DNA Dodecamer

focal_points.name: Major groove
focal_points.description: Wide, deep major groove exposing Watson-Crick base pairs for protein recognition

focal_points.name: Minor groove
focal_points.description: Narrower minor groove, target for small-molecule binding and AT-rich bending

focal_points.name: Helix termini
focal_points.description: 5' and 3' ends of the dodecamer showing blunt-end stacking geometry

composition_notes: Orient the helical axis vertically with a slight Y-rotation to show both groove depths simultaneously. Chain coloring on complementary strands maximizes visual distinction of the antiparallel duplex.

name: Hemoglobin

focal_points.name: Heme groups
focal_points.description: Four iron-containing porphyrin rings, one per subunit, each capable of binding O2

focal_points.name: Alpha-beta interface
focal_points.description: Alpha1-beta1 and alpha2-beta2 dimeric interfaces critical for cooperative oxygen binding

focal_points.name: T-state central cavity
focal_points.description: Central solvent channel between tetramers, site of 2,3-BPG allosteric regulation

composition_notes: A 45-degree Y-rotation with modest X-tilt displays the pseudo-D2 symmetry of the alpha2-beta2 tetramer. Chain coloring is essential to distinguish the four subunits in the cooperative assembly.

name: ATP Synthase

focal_points.name: F1 catalytic head
focal_points.description: Alpha3-beta3 hexameric ring with central gamma shaft; site of ATP synthesis via binding-change mechanism

focal_points.name: c-ring rotor
focal_points.description: Membrane-embedded c-subunit ring driven by proton translocation; rotation transmitted to gamma subunit

focal_points.name: Peripheral stalk
focal_points.description: b2-delta stator connecting F1 head to Fo membrane domain, preventing co-rotation

composition_notes: Orient the rotational axis vertically to convey the architectural logic of the proton turbine. Surface rendering communicates the massive scale (~530 kDa) better than cartoon at this molecular weight.

name: SARS-CoV-2 Mpro

focal_points.name: Active site cleft
focal_points.description: Catalytic dyad Cys145-His41 at the interface of domains I and II; primary drug-binding pocket

focal_points.name: Dimerization interface
focal_points.description: Domain III N-finger contact essential for productive active site geometry; dimer is the obligate form

focal_points.name: Domain III helical bundle
focal_points.description: Unique alpha-helical domain absent from related 3CLpro enzymes; allosteric regulation site

composition_notes: A 30-degree Y-rotation exposes the substrate-binding cleft between domains I and II. Secondary-structure coloring highlights the distinctive all-beta domains I/II versus the helical domain III.

name: Green Fluorescent Protein (GFP)

focal_points.name: Beta-barrel scaffold
focal_points.description: 11-stranded beta-barrel protecting the chromophore from solvent quenching

focal_points.name: Chromophore
focal_points.description: Autocatalytically formed 4-(p-hydroxybenzylidene)imidazolidin-5-one from Ser65-Tyr66-Gly67

focal_points.name: Central alpha-helix
focal_points.description: Internal helix threading the barrel axis, carrying the chromophore at its center

composition_notes: Orient the barrel axis vertically for the canonical top-down view showing 11-fold beta symmetry, or tilt 90 degrees for the side view revealing the central helix and chromophore position.

name: Insulin Hexamer

focal_points.name: Zinc coordination site
focal_points.description: Two zinc ions on the 3-fold axis, each octahedrally coordinated by His10 from three B-chains

focal_points.name: Trimer-trimer interface
focal_points.description: Hydrophobic and polar contacts between the two R3 trimers forming the hexameric assembly

focal_points.name: B-chain helix
focal_points.description: Central B-chain alpha-helix (B9-B19) forming the hexamer core and zinc ligand geometry

composition_notes: View along the C3 axis (top-down) to display the 6-fold ring symmetry; a slight X-tilt reveals the zinc sites at the central channel. Chain coloring distinguishes A and B chains across all six subunits.

name: p53-DNA Complex

focal_points.name: DNA-binding domain contact
focal_points.description: Loop-sheet-helix motif and two loops (L2, L3) inserting into DNA major groove at the response element

focal_points.name: Tetramerization domain
focal_points.description: Dimer-of-dimers interface critical for cooperative DNA binding and tumor-suppressor function

focal_points.name: Response element DNA
focal_points.description: Two half-site 5'-RRRCWWGYYY-3' repeats contacted by the p53 tetramer in the consensus response element

composition_notes: Tilt slightly along X to show both the protein tetramer and the DNA double helix in a single view. Chain coloring is critical to distinguish the four p53 subunits from the DNA strands.

name: Glutamine Synthetase

focal_points.name: Dodecameric ring
focal_points.description: Two stacked hexameric rings forming the large cylindrical assembly (~600 kDa), with 12 active sites

focal_points.name: Active site tunnels
focal_points.description: 12 bifunnel active sites at subunit interfaces, each binding two Mn2+ ions and substrates

focal_points.name: Ring-ring interface
focal_points.description: Hydrophobic contacts between the two hexameric rings with pseudo-D6 symmetry

composition_notes: View along the 6-fold symmetry axis (top-down) to reveal the double-ring architecture and the 12 active-site entrances. Surface rendering best communicates the massive cylindrical form of this 12-mer.

name: OmpF Porin

focal_points.name: Beta-barrel channels
focal_points.description: Three 18-stranded beta-barrel pores, each forming a water-filled channel for passive ion and small-molecule transport

focal_points.name: Eyelet constriction
focal_points.description: Narrowest region of each pore formed by loop L3 folding inward, size-selectivity filter (~1 nm)

focal_points.name: Trimer interface
focal_points.description: Hydrophobic membrane-facing belt and inter-monomer contacts forming the stable trimeric assembly

composition_notes: Orient perpendicular to the membrane plane (top-down view along pore axes) to show the trimeric barrel arrangement. Navy background evokes the lipid bilayer environment and improves visual contrast of beta-barrel topology.

name: Adenylate Kinase + ATP

focal_points.name: AMPbind domain
focal_points.description: Mobile substrate-binding domain for AMP; undergoes large hinge closure (~30 degrees) upon substrate binding

focal_points.name: LID domain
focal_points.description: ATP-binding lid domain covering the active site and completing the catalytic geometry upon closure

focal_points.name: CORE domain
focal_points.description: Central alpha/beta scaffold providing the fixed structural platform for the two mobile domains

composition_notes: A -40 Y-rotation exposes the hinge axis between LID and CORE domains, making the conformational change trajectory evident. This enzyme is ideal for illustrating induced-fit domain motion in catalysis.

name: CRISPR-Cas9

focal_points.name: RuvC-HNH nuclease domains
focal_points.description: Two endonuclease domains cleaving non-template and template DNA strands respectively; cleavage creates blunt DSB

focal_points.name: Guide RNA scaffold
focal_points.description: sgRNA repeat:anti-repeat duplex and nexus hairpin anchoring the guide in the recognition lobe

focal_points.name: PAM-interacting domain
focal_points.description: C-terminal PAM-interacting (PI) domain reading the 5'-NGG-3' PAM sequence for target selection

composition_notes: A 20-degree Y-rotation combined with slight X-tilt reveals the bilobed architecture (recognition lobe + nuclease lobe) and the guide RNA threading through the central channel. Chain coloring distinguishes Cas9 protein from guide RNA and target DNA.

name: Ubiquitin

focal_points.name: Beta-grasp fold
focal_points.description: Canonical beta-grasp topology with a central alpha-helix braced by a mixed beta-sheet on one face

focal_points.name: Ile44 hydrophobic patch
focal_points.description: Surface patch around Ile44, Leu8, Val70 that is the primary docking site for ubiquitin-binding domains (UBDs)

focal_points.name: C-terminal tail
focal_points.description: Gly-Gly dipeptide at the C-terminus (residues 75-76) that forms the isopeptide bond to substrate lysines

composition_notes: At only 76 residues, ubiquitin is compact enough to fill a 2x2 panel without dead space. A slight Y-rotation puts both the Ile44 patch and the C-terminal tail in the same field of view, making the functional surfaces immediately legible.

name: Hen Egg-White Lysozyme

focal_points.name: Active site cleft
focal_points.description: Deep substrate-binding groove between the alpha and beta domains housing the catalytic dyad Glu35-Asp52

focal_points.name: Alpha domain
focal_points.description: Four alpha-helices forming the larger lobe with the main hydrophobic core

focal_points.name: Beta domain
focal_points.description: Three-stranded antiparallel beta-sheet forming the smaller lobe; beta-barrel loop closes over substrate

composition_notes: A -35 Y-rotation opens the active site cleft toward the viewer, making the bilobed alpha/beta architecture and substrate groove simultaneously visible. As the first protein to have its mechanism elucidated (Phillips 1965), it remains a canonical teaching structure.

name: Myoglobin

focal_points.name: Heme group
focal_points.description: Non-covalently bound iron-porphyrin prosthetic group seated in the hydrophobic heme pocket between helices E and F

focal_points.name: Eight helices (A-H)
focal_points.description: All-alpha globin fold: eight helices forming the canonical globin scaffold first described by Kendrew in 1958

focal_points.name: Proximal His93
focal_points.description: His93 (F8) ligating the heme iron from below; distal His64 (E7) regulates O2 on-rate from above

composition_notes: Myoglobin was the first protein structure solved by X-ray crystallography (Kendrew, Nobel 1962). Secondary-structure coloring clearly delineates the eight helices. A slight X-tilt reveals the heme pocket depth. Black or Dark background lets the heme stand out as a distinct red-orange feature when ligand atom coloring is overlaid.

name: HIV-1 Protease

focal_points.name: C2-symmetric active site
focal_points.description: Catalytic Asp25-Thr26-Gly27 from each monomer form the symmetric aspartyl dyad; substrate binds across the C2 axis

focal_points.name: Flap region
focal_points.description: Two beta-hairpin flaps (residues 46-55 per monomer) that close over the active site upon substrate or inhibitor binding

focal_points.name: Homodimer interface
focal_points.description: N- and C-terminal beta-sheet strands from both monomers interdigitate to form the only tight inter-subunit contact

composition_notes: A 40-degree Y-rotation presents the C2 symmetry axis nearly perpendicular to the viewer, showing both flaps and the active site cleft in one frame. Atom coloring highlights the catalytic aspartates and any bound inhibitor against the cartoon backbone.

name: EGFR Kinase Domain

focal_points.name: ATP-binding pocket / erlotinib site
focal_points.description: Hinge region between N- and C-lobes where erlotinib binds, mimicking the adenine moiety of ATP

focal_points.name: Activation loop
focal_points.description: DFG motif and activation loop in DFG-in conformation; phospho-Tyr1068 stabilizes the active configuration

focal_points.name: N-lobe / C-lobe interface
focal_points.description: The cleft between beta-sheet N-lobe and helical C-lobe forms the catalytic site; hinge connects the two lobes

composition_notes: EGFR kinase is a premier cancer drug target (erlotinib, gefitinib). Atom coloring on the bound erlotinib ligand against a cartoon protein backbone immediately communicates the inhibitor geometry. A -30 Y-rotation opens the ATP cleft toward the viewer.

name: Cytochrome P450 3A4

focal_points.name: Heme iron / active site
focal_points.description: Iron-porphyrin heme coordinated by Cys442 as the proximal ligand; the large active site cavity above the heme can accommodate multiple substrate molecules

focal_points.name: F-G loop and access channel
focal_points.description: Flexible F-G loop region that gates substrate access to the buried active site; its conformation determines substrate selectivity

focal_points.name: I-helix
focal_points.description: Long central I-helix running above the heme plane; conserved Gly-Thr motif in the middle enables proton delivery for oxygen activation

composition_notes: CYP3A4 metabolizes ~50% of marketed drugs. Atom coloring on the heme and any bound ligand against the cartoon scaffold reveals the unusually large and malleable active site cavity. A slight Y-rotation exposes both the heme pocket and the F-G gate in a single frame.

name: PD-L1

focal_points.name: IgV-fold beta-sandwich
focal_points.description: Canonical immunoglobulin variable-domain beta-sandwich; the IgV fold is the structural basis for PD-1 recognition

focal_points.name: PD-1 binding face
focal_points.description: CC' and FG loops on the front beta-sheet that dock onto the PD-1 receptor, inhibiting T-cell activation

focal_points.name: Hydrophobic core
focal_points.description: Tightly packed hydrophobic residues between the two beta-sheets forming the thermodynamic core of the Ig fold

composition_notes: PD-L1 is a major immunotherapy checkpoint target (pembrolizumab, atezolizumab). The compact IgV fold renders well in a 2x2 panel. Secondary-structure coloring clearly delineates the two beta-sheets of the sandwich. A slight Y-rotation displays the flat binding face toward the viewer.

name: Beta2-Adrenergic GPCR

focal_points.name: Seven transmembrane helices
focal_points.description: Seven membrane-spanning alpha-helices (TM1-TM7) forming the canonical GPCR 7TM bundle; carazolol binds in the orthosteric pocket

focal_points.name: Orthosteric binding pocket
focal_points.description: Ligand-binding pocket between TM3, TM5, TM6 and TM7 where carazolol (inverse agonist) is coordinated

focal_points.name: Intracellular G-protein coupling face
focal_points.description: Intracellular face with ICL2 and ICL3 loops and TM5/TM6 cytoplasmic ends that engage the Gs heterotrimer

composition_notes: Beta2AR was the first GPCR crystallized (Kobilka and Lefkowitz, Nobel 2012). Surface rendering communicates the membrane-spanning architecture. Navy background evokes the lipid bilayer. A 20-degree Y-rotation reveals both the extracellular binding pocket and the intracellular G-protein interface.

name: KcsA K+ Channel

focal_points.name: Selectivity filter
focal_points.description: TVGYG sequence forming the 12-angstrom-long selectivity filter that selects K+ over Na+ with high fidelity

focal_points.name: Inner helix bundle gate
focal_points.description: Four inner helices crossing below the selectivity filter to form the hydrophobic gate; helix bending opens the channel

focal_points.name: Outer (pore) helices
focal_points.description: Four outer helices flanking the selectivity filter that provide the structural scaffold for the narrow ion pathway

composition_notes: KcsA (MacKinnon, Nobel 2003) defined the structural basis of ion selectivity. View along the channel axis (top-down) to display the C4 symmetry and the selectivity filter entrance. Navy background places the channel in membrane context. Chain coloring distinguishes the four identical subunits of the homotetramer.

name: tRNA-Phe

focal_points.name: L-shaped tertiary fold
focal_points.description: The classic L-shape formed by stacking of the acceptor stem on the T-arm and the anticodon stem on the D-arm

focal_points.name: Anticodon loop
focal_points.description: 7-nucleotide anticodon loop at one end of the L presenting the GAA anticodon for mRNA codon recognition

focal_points.name: 3'-CCA acceptor end
focal_points.description: Single-stranded 3'-CCA terminus at the other end of the L where Phe is aminoacylated by PheRS

composition_notes: tRNA-Phe is the reference RNA tertiary fold. Stick representation shows the ribose-phosphate backbone and base stacking clearly. A -30 Y-rotation with slight X-tilt displays the full L-shape in one frame. Chain coloring on the single chain uses positional coloring to show the 5'-to-3' fold-back geometry.

name: Nucleosome Core Particle

focal_points.name: Histone octamer core
focal_points.description: (H3-H4)2 tetramer flanked by two H2A-H2B dimers; the octamer presents a positively charged surface for DNA wrapping

focal_points.name: 147 bp DNA superhelix
focal_points.description: 146-147 bp of DNA wrapping 1.65 turns around the octamer in a left-handed superhelix at 28 angstrom diameter

focal_points.name: Histone tails
focal_points.description: Unstructured N-terminal tails of H3 and H4 passing between the DNA gyres; post-translational modification sites

composition_notes: The nucleosome core particle (Luger et al. 1997) is the fundamental unit of eukaryotic chromatin compaction. Chain coloring is essential to distinguish the eight histone subunits from each other and from the two DNA strands. Stick rendering for the DNA combined with cartoon for the histones shows both components at appropriate detail.

name: GroEL-GroES Chaperonin

focal_points.name: GroEL double-ring barrel
focal_points.description: Two heptameric GroEL rings stacked back-to-back forming the large barrel; each ring has a central cavity for substrate folding

focal_points.name: GroES dome cap
focal_points.description: Heptameric GroES co-chaperonin capping one GroEL ring, enclosing the folding chamber and releasing substrate upon ATP hydrolysis

focal_points.name: Apical substrate-binding domains
focal_points.description: Apical domains of the uncapped GroEL ring exposing hydrophobic surfaces that bind unfolded substrate proteins

composition_notes: GroEL-GroES is the quintessential molecular chaperone machine (~900 kDa). Surface rendering at a large camera distance conveys the iconic football shape. A slight X-tilt off the 7-fold axis shows both the capped and uncapped GroEL rings simultaneously. Chain coloring distinguishes the 14 GroEL and 7 GroES subunits.

name: 26S Proteasome

focal_points.name: 20S core particle barrel
focal_points.description: Four stacked heptameric rings (alpha7-beta7-beta7-alpha7) forming the proteolytic barrel; threonine active sites face the inner chamber

focal_points.name: 19S regulatory cap (lid + base)
focal_points.description: One or two 19S caps docking on alpha-ring faces; base contains AAA-ATPase ring that unfolds and translocates ubiquitinated substrates

focal_points.name: Ubiquitin receptor subunits
focal_points.description: Rpn10 and Rpn13 in the 19S lid function as ubiquitin receptors that recognize polyubiquitin chains on substrates

composition_notes: The 26S proteasome (~2.5 MDa) is among the largest asymmetric complexes in the PDB. Surface rendering at maximum camera distance is required to fit the full assembly. A slight Y-rotation reveals the asymmetric cap(s) alongside the symmetric 20S barrel core. Chain coloring distinguishes the many subunits and communicates the modular architecture.

name: RNA Polymerase II

focal_points.name: Clamp and cleft
focal_points.description: Mobile clamp domain closing over the DNA-RNA hybrid in the active site cleft; clamp opening/closing is key to translocation

focal_points.name: Active site with Mg2+ bridge
focal_points.description: Two magnesium ions coordinated by the universally conserved DFDGD motif in Rpb1; site of phosphodiester bond formation

focal_points.name: Rpb4/Rpb7 stalk
focal_points.description: Dissociable Rpb4-Rpb7 heterodimer protruding from the main body; important for initiation and stress response

composition_notes: RNA Pol II (Kornberg, Nobel 2006) is the engine of eukaryotic gene expression. Surface rendering of the 12-subunit, 500 kDa complex communicates scale and modular organization. A -20 Y-rotation opens the DNA entry cleft toward the viewer. Chain coloring distinguishes the 12 subunits (Rpb1-Rpb12).

name: IgG1 Antibody

focal_points.name: CDR loops (antigen-binding site)
focal_points.description: Six complementarity-determining region loops (H1-H3, L1-L3) at the Fab tips forming the hypervariable antigen-binding surface

focal_points.name: Fab arms
focal_points.description: Two identical Fab fragments (VH-CH1 / VL-CL domain pairs) articulated by the flexible hinge region

focal_points.name: Fc region
focal_points.description: CH2-CH3 domain pair at the base; binds Fc receptors and complement to mediate effector functions

composition_notes: Chain coloring is essential for IgG to distinguish the two heavy chains from the two light chains, making the Y-shaped architecture legible. The flexible hinge means the two Fabs may be asymmetrically positioned; a slight Y-rotation shows both Fab tips and the Fc stem in a single view. Camera at 1.9 fits the full Y-shape without cropping.

name: SARS-CoV-2 Spike Trimer

focal_points.name: Receptor-binding domain (RBD)
focal_points.description: One RBD in 'up' conformation (ACE2-accessible) and two in 'down' in the asymmetric prefusion trimer; primary neutralizing antibody target

focal_points.name: N-terminal domain (NTD)
focal_points.description: Beta-barrel NTDs flanking each RBD; target of class IV neutralizing antibodies and site of many immune-evasion mutations

focal_points.name: Fusion peptide / S2 stalk
focal_points.description: Central helical coiled-coil S2 stalk in prefusion conformation; dramatic refolding drives membrane fusion upon receptor binding

composition_notes: The SARS-CoV-2 spike trimer is the defining structure of the pandemic era. Surface rendering and a gradient-dark background emphasize its menacing scale and globular form. Chain coloring distinguishes the three protomers (A/B/C), making the trimer symmetry and the asymmetric RBD up/down state immediately visible.

name: Beta2AR-Gs Complex

focal_points.name: GPCR 7TM bundle
focal_points.description: Beta2-adrenergic receptor transmembrane helices in active conformation with TM6 outward displacement exposing the G-protein binding cavity

focal_points.name: Gs alpha5 helix insertion
focal_points.description: C-terminal alpha5 helix of Gsalpha inserting into the intracellular cavity of the receptor; primary coupling interface

focal_points.name: Gs heterotrimer
focal_points.description: Gsalpha (Ras-like + helical domain), Gsbeta, and Gsgamma forming the full heterotrimer engaged with the receptor

composition_notes: Beta2AR-Gs (Kobilka, Nobel 2012) was the first GPCR-G protein complex structure. Surface rendering at a slightly elevated camera distance fits both the 7TM receptor and the G-protein heterotrimer. Navy background evokes the membrane environment. Chain coloring distinguishes receptor, Gsalpha, Gsbeta, and Gsgamma.

name: Collagen Triple Helix

focal_points.name: Triple-helical supercoil
focal_points.description: Three polyproline II-like left-handed helices coiled into a right-handed superhelix; the canonical collagen fold

focal_points.name: Gly at every third position
focal_points.description: Glycine at every third residue (Gly-X-Y repeat) packs at the central axis; any substitution causes disease (osteogenesis imperfecta)

focal_points.name: Hydroxyproline stabilization
focal_points.description: 4-hydroxyproline in the Y position forms water-mediated hydrogen bonds that thermally stabilize the triple helix

composition_notes: Collagen is the most abundant protein in the human body. The rod-like triple helix is best displayed with the helical axis oriented vertically in a 1x2 panel, showing the three chains coiling together along the full length. Chain coloring with three distinct colors makes the individual chains and their interdigitation immediately legible.

name: F-Actin Filament

focal_points.name: Double-stranded helical polymer
focal_points.description: Two actin strands forming a right-handed double helix with a 37 nm crossover repeat; the basic cytoskeletal fiber

focal_points.name: Barbed (+) end
focal_points.description: Fast-growing barbed end where actin-ATP monomers preferentially add; target of profilin and barbed-end cappers

focal_points.name: Pointed (-) end
focal_points.description: Slow-growing pointed end where ADP-actin preferentially dissociates, driving treadmilling dynamics

composition_notes: F-actin filament cryo-EM structure shows the polymer that drives cell motility and muscle contraction. Display the filament axis vertically in a 1x2 panel to show multiple protomers of the helical repeat. Surface rendering at a moderate camera distance communicates the polymer scale. Chain coloring with alternating colors helps trace each strand of the double helix.

name: Streptavidin-Biotin

focal_points.name: Biotin binding pocket
focal_points.description: Deep hydrophobic barrel pocket in each monomer where biotin binds with Kd ~10^-15 M; loop 3-4 closes over biotin upon binding

focal_points.name: Beta-barrel tetramer
focal_points.description: Four eight-stranded beta-barrels packed into a D2-symmetric tetramer with two pseudo-dyad axes

focal_points.name: Binding loop (loop 3-4)
focal_points.description: Flexible loop that folds over the bound biotin, accounting for much of the extreme binding affinity through extensive van der Waals and hydrogen bond contacts

composition_notes: Streptavidin-biotin is the strongest known non-covalent biological interaction and a cornerstone of biotechnology. Chain coloring distinguishes the four subunits of the homotetramer. A slight X-tilt reveals all four binding pockets. Atom coloring on the biotin ligands against the cartoon protein provides an immediate visual indication of each occupied pocket.

name: Cas12a / Cpf1

focal_points.name: Crescent-shaped architecture
focal_points.description: Distinctive crescent or comma shape formed by the recognition (REC) lobe and nuclease (NUC) lobe; different from the bilobed Cas9

focal_points.name: RuvC nuclease domain
focal_points.description: Single RuvC domain that cleaves both strands sequentially, generating 5-nt 5'-overhangs rather than blunt cuts

focal_points.name: PAM-interacting / WED domain
focal_points.description: WED and PI domains recognizing the T-rich PAM on the non-target strand at the 5' end of the protospacer

composition_notes: Cas12a (Cpf1) generates 5-overhang cuts and requires only a crRNA (no tracrRNA), making it attractive for multiplex editing. Chain coloring distinguishes the protein from the crRNA guide. A -25 Y-rotation displays the distinctive crescent profile that differentiates Cas12a from Cas9.

name: Kinesin Motor Domain

focal_points.name: Switch I/Switch II nucleotide-binding site
focal_points.description: P-loop, switch I, and switch II elements around the bound ADP/ATP that couple nucleotide state to neck linker docking

focal_points.name: Neck linker
focal_points.description: C-terminal neck linker that docks onto the motor domain in the ATP state, generating the ~8 nm hand-over-hand step

focal_points.name: Microtubule-binding interface
focal_points.description: Loop L8, helix alpha4, and loop L12 forming the tubulin contact surface; microtubule binding accelerates ATPase 1000-fold

composition_notes: Kinesin is the canonical processive cytoskeletal motor. Secondary-structure coloring clearly delineates the central beta-sheet core and surrounding helices. A -20 Y-rotation places the neck linker and the MT-binding face visible simultaneously, conveying the mechanochemical cycle.

name: Taq DNA Polymerase

focal_points.name: Thumb, palm, and fingers subdomains
focal_points.description: Right-hand topology with thumb gripping DNA duplex, palm containing the catalytic DDD triad, and fingers closing over incoming dNTP

focal_points.name: 5'-to-3' exonuclease domain
focal_points.description: N-terminal 5'-to-3' exonuclease domain unique among thermostable polymerases; used in TaqMan probe hydrolysis assays

focal_points.name: O-helix (finger closing)
focal_points.description: Conserved O-helix in the fingers subdomain that swings inward upon correct dNTP binding, triggering the induced-fit conformational change

composition_notes: Taq polymerase is the PCR workhorse. The right-hand fold metaphor (thumb, palm, fingers) is one of the most pedagogically useful in structural biology. A -30 Y-rotation opens the DNA-binding cleft toward the viewer, making the three subdomains clearly distinguishable. Secondary-structure coloring delineates the domain architecture.

name: p53 DNA-Binding Domain

focal_points.name: Zinc-coordinated L2/L3 loops
focal_points.description: Zinc ion tetrahedrally coordinated by Cys176, His179, Cys238, Cys242 stabilizing the L2 and L3 loops that contact DNA

focal_points.name: Loop-sheet-helix motif
focal_points.description: Key DNA-contact element: L1 loop, S2-S2' hairpin, and helix H2 insert into the DNA major groove at the response element

focal_points.name: Hotspot mutation residues
focal_points.description: Arg175, Gly245, Arg248, Arg249, Arg273, Arg282 — six hotspot positions mutated in >30% of all human cancers

composition_notes: p53 DBD is mutated in more than half of all human tumors. Atom coloring highlights the zinc ion and coordinating residues in context of the cartoon scaffold. A -20 Y-rotation reveals the DNA-contacting loops and the helix H2 insertion element together. This is the monomer reference; see 3PQR for the full tetramer-DNA complex.
